nodes.description: Address state variable in Owned holding the privileged owner account
Address state variable in Owned holding the pending new owner during two-step ownership transfer
Public token symbol string 'BST'
Public token name string 'Bit Shopper Token'
Public uint8 token decimals (18)
Public total token supply set in the constructor
Mapping(address => uint) of token balances, written by transfer/transferFrom and the constructor
Nested mapping(address => mapping(address => uint)) of allowances, written by approve and approveAndCall
SafeMath.safeAdd(uint a, uint b) pure; adds and requires c >= a to detect overflow
SafeMath.safeSub(uint a, uint b) pure; requires b <= a before subtracting
SafeMath.safeMul(uint a, uint b) pure; multiplies and requires a == 0 || c / a == b
SafeMath.safeDiv(uint a, uint b) pure; requires b > 0 before dividing
Owned constructor that assigns owner = msg.sender
Owned.transferOwnership(address _newOwner) with onlyOwner modifier; stages newOwner
Owned.acceptOwnership() requiring msg.sender == newOwner; finalizes ownership change
Token constructor initializing metadata, minting the whole supply to a fixed address and emitting Transfer
Returns _totalSupply - balances[address(0)] using an unchecked subtraction
Returns balances[tokenOwner] for a given address
ERC20 transfer; debits msg.sender via safeSub and credits 'to' via safeAdd without any allowance check
ERC20 approve; writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] = tokens with no zero-address or race protection
ERC20 transferFrom; uses safeSub for both balance and allowance and safeAdd for the recipient
Constant function returning allowed[tokenOwner][spender]
Sets an allowance then invokes receiveApproval on the spender contract with attacker-supplied data
Payable fallback function that unconditionally reverts, refusing plain ETH
onlyOwner rescue function that calls transfer(owner, tokens) on an arbitrary token contract
Caller-controlled address used as owner, balance holder, spender and allowance owner; sole untrusted input in this contract
External call ApproveAndCallFallBack(spender).receiveApproval(msg.sender, tokens, this, data) to an untrusted contract
External call ERC20Interface(tokenAddress).transfer(owner, tokens) to an arbitrary caller-supplied token contract
Unchecked subtraction _totalSupply - balances[address(0)] in totalSupply(), not routed through SafeMath

edges.reason: msg.sender is assigned to the owner state variable in the Owned constructor, granting the privileged role to the deployer/caller
Owned constructor writes the owner state variable
onlyOwner modifier requires msg.sender == owner before transferOwnership body executes
transferOwnership writes the newOwner state variable
_newOwner parameter flows into the newOwner state variable
acceptOwnership requires msg.sender == newOwner, caller-controlled authorization check
acceptOwnership sets owner = newOwner
acceptOwnership resets newOwner to address(0)
constructor writes the symbol state variable
constructor writes the name state variable
constructor writes the decimals state variable
constructor writes _totalSupply
constructor mints the entire supply into balances of the fixed address
totalSupply() reads _totalSupply
totalSupply() reads balances[address(0)] as a burn adjustment
totalSupply() performs an unchecked uint subtraction that is not routed through SafeMath
balanceOf() reads the balances mapping
tokenOwner parameter is used to index balances in balanceOf()
msg.sender is the debited account in transfer()
transfer() writes balances[msg.sender] and balances[to] before returning
transfer() delegates the sender balance subtraction to safeSub
transfer() delegates the recipient balance addition to safeAdd
to parameter is the recipient of transfer()
tokens parameter is the amount moved by transfer()
approve() writes allowed[msg.sender][spender]
msg.sender owns the allowance slot written by approve()
spender parameter receives the allowance without any zero-address validation
tokens parameter becomes the allowance value, overriding the previous allowance
transferFrom() updates balances[from] and balances[to]
transferFrom() decrements allowed[from][msg.sender]
transferFrom() uses safeSub for both the balance and the allowance
transferFrom() uses safeAdd to credit the recipient
from parameter is the debited account in transferFrom()
to parameter is the credited account in transferFrom()
tokens parameter is the transferred amount in transferFrom()
msg.sender is the spender whose allowance is consumed in transferFrom()
allowance() reads the allowed mapping
tokenOwner parameter selects the allowance owner in allowance()
spender parameter selects the spender in allowance()
approveAndCall() writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] before the external call
msg.sender is the approval owner used in approveAndCall()
spender parameter is attacker-controlled and selects the contract that will be called
tokens parameter sets the allowance and is forwarded to the callee
arbitrary bytes data parameter is accepted with no validation
approveAndCall() performs an external call to ApproveAndCallFallBack(spender).receiveApproval with controller-supplied data
spender parameter is the target address of the untrusted external call
attacker-controlled data is passed through to the external contract call
A malicious spender contract can re-enter token functions (transfer/approve/transferFrom) from inside receiveApproval before the caller returns
onlyOwner restricts transferAnyERC20Token to the caller satisfying msg.sender == owner
transferAnyERC20Token performs an external call on an arbitrary token contract
tokenAddress parameter selects the rescue target
tokens parameter is the amount forwarded to the external token transfer
tokenAddress value is used as the callee address of the external ERC20 transfer
recovered tokens are always sent to the owner state variable address

normalization_plan.reason: The 'to' parameter only describes the recipient used by transfer; it has no independent semantic role, so it merges into the transfer function node
The tokens amount parameter is fully consumed by transfer's balance updates and merges into the transfer function node
The spender parameter only exists to index the allowed mapping inside approve, so it merges into the approve function node
The tokens parameter is only the value written by approve and merges into the approve function node
The from address parameter is only used to debit balances inside transferFrom and merges into that function node
The to address parameter is only used to credit balances inside transferFrom and merges into that function node
The tokens parameter is only the amount transferred by transferFrom and merges into that function node
The tokenOwner parameter is only a lookup key in allowance and merges into the allowance function node
The spender parameter is only a lookup key in allowance and merges into the allowance function node
The tokenOwner parameter is only the mapping key of balanceOf and merges into the balanceOf function node
The spender parameter is both the allowance key and the external call target of approveAndCall, so it merges into that function node
The tokens parameter is only the allowance amount and forwarded value inside approveAndCall and merges into that function node
The data parameter is only forwarded to the external receiveApproval call made by approveAndCall, so it merges into that function node
The tokenAddress parameter is only the external call target of transferAnyERC20Token and merges into that function node
The tokens parameter is only the amount forwarded by transferAnyERC20Token and merges into that function node
The _newOwner parameter is directly stored into the newOwner state variable by transferOwnership, so it merges into that function node
